shipped_rows.title_o: Cerebral dominance for language function in adults with specific language impairment or autism

blind_target.title: Handedness and specific language impairment: A study of 6-year-old twins
blind_target.evidence_quote: In an attempt to replicate the previously reported relationship between language disorder and a reduced tendency to reach across the midline (Bishop, 2005; E. L. Hill & Bishop, 1998), we also assessed whether the probability of reaching to the seven spatial positions in the QHP task differed between the DLD and TD groups.
blind_target.outcome_quote: In particular, our failure to replicate a between-groups difference in the probability of reaching across the midline with the right hand indicates that this may not be a marker of compromised neurodevelopment relevant to language disorder, as previously suggested (Bishop, 2005; E. L. Hill & Bishop, 1998).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The corresponding published association is tested in the new twin sample and is not supported.

blind_target.authors: Illingworth, S., & Bishop, D. V. M.
blind_target.title: Atypical cerebral lateralisation in adults with compensated developmental dyslexia demonstrated using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound
blind_target.evidence_quote: We aimed to replicate previous findings of an association between DLD and reduced laterality on a quantitative measure of hand preference (reaching across the midline) and on language laterality assessed using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound.
blind_target.outcome_quote: There was no difference between the DLD and TD groups on quantitative measures of handedness or language lateralisation, or on a categorical measure of consistency of left hemisphere dominance.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The corresponding published association is tested in the new twin sample and is not supported.

blind_target.authors: Groen, M., Whitehouse, A. J. O., Badcock, N. A., & Bishop, D. V.
blind_target.title: Does cerebral lateralization develop? A study using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound assessing lateralization for language production and visuospatial memory
blind_target.evidence_quote: A subsidiary aim was to see whether we could replicate associations between language laterality and language tests found by Groen et al. (2012).
blind_target.outcome_quote: In the second step of analysis, we tested the relationship between language and laterality from the opposite direction, using language measures as predictors, aiming to replicate the effects reported by Groen et al. (2012). We computed Spearman's correlations between each language measure and the fTCD laterality index in the two replication samples. However, no uncorrected correlation replicated across samples, and no correlation within a sample survived a Holm-Bonferroni correction.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The corresponding published association is tested in the new twin sample and is not supported.

Its sample tests DLD-related language laterality; the cited reference identifies this original report.

hemisphere dominance for language may be a neurobiological correlate of language problems 

(e.g. Annett, 2002; Bishop, 2013; T. J. Crow et al., 1998), and empirical studies of very small 

samples have supported that view (Illingworth & Bishop, 2009; Whitehouse & Bishop, 2008).
